QEMU absolute M5.begin times (~600/950 ms) are not hardware measurements; only head/base deltas are meaningful

notes: PR left OPEN; one English comment planned; no close, no push, no change to m5stack/M5Unified.
Primary evidence is virtual-device validation of the absent-device path on basic-v27 and nanoc6, plus code-level verification of the CoreP4X rail sequencing and P4 compilation.
The virtual boards have no LSM6DS3TR-C, so the sensor-present register path is NOT RUN; this is the main remaining gap and matches the author's own untested CoreP4X case.

Non-blocking observations: (1) when the new wait fires and the LSM is present, the driver still waits 15 ms + 1 tick, so that narrow path is ~15 ms slower than before; (2) the new waits use exactly 15 ms while the driver uses 15 ms + 1 tick, and a failed first probe is not retried.
Firmware images are recorded by SHA256 and size; binaries themselves are not committed.
